scenarios.title: Ground a conversion goal in an advertiser event source
scenarios.given: The buyer asks for a conversion-optimized campaign and has named the advertiser and outcome.
expect: The agent searches the advertiser's event sources before saving the conversion goal.
The agent reuses or registers an exact event source and puts the source's eventSourceId in the campaign goal.
The agent reports source health separately and omits the goal if the buyer explicitly skips conversion tracking.

scenarios.title: Disclose Meta REACH default frequency cap before staging
scenarios.given: The buyer selects the meta_awareness product and has not specified a frequency cap.
expect: The agent discloses that Meta automatically applies a 2-impressions-per-7-days default frequency cap for the meta_awareness (REACH optimization) product.
The agent asks the buyer whether to use the default or specify a different cap before staging the media buy.
If the buyer requests an override, the agent includes targetingOverlay.frequency_cap with the correct max_impressions and window fields in the save_media_buy call.

scenarios.title: Turn a site-traffic outcome into a seller-counted goal statement
scenarios.given: The buyer says "find dog lovers in Slovenia, get them to my online store, €5,000" and has no event source or analytics tracker.
expect: The agent asks how the buyer will know it worked and who can count that result before saving any goal.

The agent proposes a one-line goal statement (clicks, a cost-per-click target the buyer names, counted by the seller's ad server, the commitment the buyer wants) and saves only the confirmed goal as a metric goal in optimizationGoals and the confirmed cost-per-click target as bidding.cost_per with the strength the buyer confirms.
The agent offers campaign click-URL parameters through save_campaign tracking.macroAdditions so the buyer's own analytics can attribute the visits, and does not add them without confirmation.

scenarios.title: Ground a purchase goal counted by the buyer's own tracking
scenarios.given: The buyer wants online sales, says they use a website pixel, and has named the advertiser.
expect: The agent searches the advertiser's event sources and reuses or registers an exact event source before saving the goal.

The agent proposes a goal statement counted by the buyer's event source and saves a confirmed event goal with the source's eventSourceId, and puts a cost or return target the buyer names in bidding rather than on the goal.
The agent tells the buyer, from the goal-seeking campaigns page, that a seller can only aim for an event goal unless it can read the buyer's events.

scenarios.title: Handle a vendor-measured store-visit outcome without inventing a goal kind
scenarios.given: The buyer wants store visits and says a footfall measurement vendor counts them.
expect: The agent retrieves the goal-seeking campaigns page and follows its current rule for vendor-measured goals instead of inventing a vendor goal kind.
The agent puts the store-visit outcome and the vendor in the campaign brief and does not write a structured vendor goal to optimizationGoals.
The agent tells the buyer what the platform does and does not do with a vendor-measured outcome today, as the page states.

scenarios.title: Proceed on the brief when the buyer declines to set a goal
scenarios.given: The buyer is asked how they will know the campaign worked and says they do not want to set a goal.
expect: The agent saves the campaign without optimizationGoals and does not infer a goal from the campaign name or brief.
The agent explains, from the page's section on campaigns without a goal, that sellers price against the brief alone and proposals answer no goal of theirs.
The agent continues to request proposals only after the usual confirmation.

scenarios.title: Compare proposals on the goal's terms
scenarios.given: A campaign with a clicks goal at a €3 cost-per-click target and a stated wish for a guaranteed price has a terminal proposal round with a guaranteed, a best-effort and a report-only answer, and one seller that declined.
expect: Before requesting proposals, the agent restates the goal statement and the commitment wanted and asks for confirmation.
The agent groups sellers by commitment.kind and commitment.meetsAskedTarget read from each proposal, names the answered target for each, and lists the seller that declined.
The agent never presents the best-effort answer as a guarantee or as cheaper than the guaranteed one on price alone, and ties its recommendation to the commitment the buyer wanted.

scenarios.title: Upload HTML5 ZIPs, finish the drafts, then attach them
scenarios.given: The buyer has five HTML5 ZIP banners on disk for an existing advertiser and wants them on the campaign.
expect: The agent retrieves the HTML5 creative requirements page and checks each ZIP's click tag, declared size and size limit with the buyer before uploading.

The agent uploads each ZIP with upload_creative_asset for the exact advertiser, then finishes each returned draft with save_creative mode "complete" and the buyer's landing_page_url, with no campaign.

The agent attaches only complete creatives to the campaign, after confirmation, and reports each creative as uploaded, complete or attached only after a get confirms it; a failed upload is reported as not saved, never as a saved draft.

scenarios.title: Report creative review on a draft campaign without implying it is running
scenarios.given: The campaign is in phase draft with two draft media buys, and its four creatives read pending_review.
expect: The agent says the campaign is a draft, its media buys are not booked and nothing delivers until it is launched.

The agent explains that the creatives were sent to the draft buys' sellers when saved, reads platformLinks to name which seller holds each creative, and presents pending_review as that seller's creative review, not a booking.
The agent names the launch as the next confirmation and does not launch without it.

scenarios.title: Offer a connected Drive or SharePoint file without browsing it
scenarios.given: The buyer says their product spreadsheet lives in a Google Drive folder their account has connected, and wants it as the advertiser's catalog. They have not given a connection ID or file ID.
expect: The agent sends the buyer to the Catalogs page in the Apostra app to pick the file from its "Connected folder" source, and does not claim it can list or open their folders or files.
The agent does not invent a sourceId or itemId, and calls save_catalog with file only if the buyer gives both IDs.
If the buyer's account has no connected folder, the agent says connected folders are in early access and offers a feed URL or items instead.
